train: The instrument typically features a flared bell at one end that helps project sound.
A long, cylindrical tube is coiled into a compact shape, aiding in portability.
Valves are used to alter the pitch by redirecting the airflow through different tubing.
The mouthpiece is a small, cup-shaped piece that allows the player to produce sound.
Brass is the primary material used in construction, providing durability and a bright tone.
The instrument often has a series of slides or valves that help adjust the pitch.
Some variants include a detachable bell that can be replaced for different tonal qualities.
The overall length of the instrument can vary, influencing the range of notes produced.
